schema_note:
Single source of truth for the literature database.

Run:  python3 build_database.py
Writes literature_database.json and literature_matrix.csv next to this file.

Page convention: "PDF p.X / p.Y" = page X of the PDF file / printed journal page Y.
Batch 2 records (P6-P9) live in papers_batch2.py.
Page maps:  P1 printed = PDF+58 | P2 printed = PDF+1255 | P3 printed = PDF+137
            P4 printed = PDF+3084 | P5 printed = PDF+85 (PDF p.1 is a cover sheet)
Every field was extracted from the PDFs in ../papers/. Items marked
"[INFERENCE]" are reviewer judgements, not statements made by the authors.

papers.title: Cong bo thong tin trach nhiem xa hoi va chi phi von co phan: bang chung thuc nghiem tu cac doanh nghiep Viet Nam (Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure and Cost of Equity Capital: Empirical Evidence from Vietnamese Enterprises)
authors: Le Thi Nhung (Academy of Policy and Development)
papers.source: Tap chi Khoa hoc Thuong mai (Journal of Trade Science), No. 187/2024, pp. 61-71 (Vietnamese)
papers.page_map: printed page = PDF page + 58 (PDF pp.1-2 are the issue table of contents)
papers.topic: CSR disclosure and cost of equity
papers.research_question: Does the level of CSR disclosure affect the cost of equity of Vietnamese listed firms? [PDF p.4 / p.62]
papers.abstract: Panel of 93 VNR500 (2021) listed non-financial firms, 2014-2021; CAPM cost of equity; content-analysis CSR disclosure index; firms with higher CSR disclosure scores have lower cost of equity. [PDF p.3 / p.61]
theory: Information asymmetry / disclosure-cost of capital (liquidity, estimation risk, public vs private information) [PDF p.5 / p.63]
Risk-reduction view of CSR vs over-investment/agency-cost view of CSR (presented, not tested against each other) [PDF p.4-5 / p.62-63]
Signalling invoked in conclusion [PDF p.12 / p.70]
hypotheses: H1: negative relation between CSR disclosure and cost of equity [PDF p.6 / p.64]
papers.data_source: Annual, sustainability and CSR reports (hand-coded); prices, VNINDEX and 1-year government bond yields from Investing.com [PDF p.6 / p.64]
papers.sample: 93 of the VNR500-2021 firms listed on HOSE/HNX, excl. finance/banking, with at least one annual/SD/CSR report and full audited FS 2014-2021; 744 firm-years [PDF p.6 / p.64]
dependent_vars: Re: CAPM cost of equity; Rf = 1-year government bond; annual beta vs VNINDEX; market risk premium = average 2014-2021 VNINDEX return minus 1-year bond [PDF p.6-7 / p.64-65]
independent_vars: CSRI: 0/1 coding of 33 items derived from Circular 155/2015/TT-BTC (environment 18, labour 10, community 5), score/33 [Table 1, PDF p.7-8 / p.65-66]
papers.method: Pooled OLS, FEM, REM; Hausman (p=0.0002) and F-test (p=0.0001) select FEM; GLS reported as final model [Tables 6-8, PDF p.10-11 / p.68-69]
papers.econometric_model: Re_it = b1 + b2*CSRI_it + bj*X_it + mu_i + e_it [PDF p.9 / p.67]
main_findings: CSRI -6.012*** in GLS (N=744) [Table 8, PDF p.11 / p.69]
SIZE -2.230*, LEV +0.795***, BTM +2.134**, GROWTH n.s. [Table 8]
Mean Re 14.251%; mean CSRI 0.432 [Table 3, PDF p.9 / p.67]
robustness: None reported beyond the switch from FEM to GLS
limitations_explicit: Examines only the aggregate CSR-disclosure effect [PDF p.13 / p.71]
future_research: Effects of specific CSR dimensions on cost of equity [PDF p.13 / p.71]
reviewer_flags: Table 3: reported SD of CSRI (4.172) and LEV (2.194) exceed their own min-max ranges (0.048-0.895; 0.218-0.839), which is arithmetically impossible [PDF p.9 / p.67]
Table 7: heteroskedasticity p=0.2351 and autocorrelation p=0.3065 do not reject the nulls, yet the text says both problems are present and switches to GLS [PDF p.11 / p.69]
Table 8: the figures in parentheses are unlabelled; CSRI (-0.09) cannot be a t-statistic consistent with *** [PDF p.11 / p.69]
Text gives mean VIF 1.29; Table 5 gives 1.25 [PDF p.10 / p.68]
The FEM coefficient on CSRI (the Hausman-preferred model) is never reported
[INFERENCE] The 2014-2021 window is chosen as 'before and after Circular 155' [PDF p.6 / p.64], but no pre/post or DiD test is run
[INFERENCE] A constant market risk premium means cross-sectional COE variation comes only from beta; year-to-year variation comes from the 1-year Rf
[INFERENCE] Sampling on the 2021 VNR500 list is look-ahead/survivorship selection
[INFERENCE] Disclosure for year t comes out in the annual report in t+1, while beta is estimated from year-t returns (timing mismatch)

papers.title: The impact of sustainability reporting on the cost of capital: evidence from Vietnam's listed companies
authors: Hien Khanh Duong (University of Economics, The University of Da Nang)
papers.source: Journal of Financial Reporting and Accounting, Vol. 24 No. 3, pp. 1256-1280 (Emerald); received Sep 2024, accepted Jan 2025
papers.topic: GRI-based sustainability (SDG) disclosure and cost of debt, cost of equity and WACC
papers.research_question: RQ1-RQ3: does sustainable-development disclosure affect COD, COE and WACC? [PDF p.3 / p.1258]
papers.abstract: Top-100 listed firms by market cap (31 Dec 2023), 2021-2023; sustainability disclosure is negatively related to COD, COE and WACC; environmental SDG disclosures have the largest effect. [PDF p.1 / p.1256]
theory: Signalling theory (declared the 'most foundational') [PDF p.5 / p.1260]
hypotheses: H1: SD disclosure negatively related to COE [PDF p.5 / p.1260]
H2: SD disclosure negatively related to COD [PDF p.6 / p.1261]
H3: SD disclosure negatively related to WACC [PDF p.6 / p.1261]
papers.data_source: Annual reports, FS, ESG and sustainability reports (hand-coded); beta and market risk premium from Vietstock; bond yields from the Ministry of Finance [PDF p.6-7 / p.1261-1262]
papers.sample: 100 largest listed firms by market capitalisation at 31 Dec 2023 (~90% of market cap), 2021-2023; 300 firm-years [PDF p.6 / p.1261]
papers.industry: Multi-industry (exclusion of financial firms not stated)
dependent_vars: COE: CAPM, Rf = 10-year government bond [PDF p.7 / p.1262]
COD: interest expense / total liabilities [PDF p.7 / p.1262]
WACC: book weights, effective tax rate [PDF p.8 / p.1263]
independent_vars: SDG: average of 77 binary GRI (2016) items [PDF p.8 / p.1263]
Sub-indices SDG-environment, SDG-economy, SDG-society [Table 6, PDF p.15 / p.1270]
papers.method: OLS, FEM, REM; F-test and Hausman; GLS to correct autocorrelation/heteroskedasticity [PDF p.7 / p.1262]
papers.econometric_model: Y_it = b0 + b1*SDG_it + controls + e_it, Y in {COE, COD, WACC} [Eqs 1-3, PDF p.7 / p.1262]
main_findings: Environment sub-index significant for COE (-0.090***), COD (-0.013***) and WACC (-0.025***); social sub-index for COD and WACC only; economic n.s. [Table 6, PDF p.15 / p.1270]
GOV lowers COE (-0.014*); IND (ESI) lowers WACC (-0.015***) [Tables 3, 5]
robustness: Decomposition by GRI dimension, labelled a 'robust test' [Table 6, PDF p.14-15 / p.1269-1270]
limitations_explicit: Consistency of the 77-item scoring across firms' reporting styles [PDF p.16 / p.1271]
COD measured as interest/total debt rather than actual loan rates [PDF p.16 / p.1271]
future_research: Longer time frame; broader sample and industries; address endogeneity; lagged variables; alternative COE methods; actual loan rates [PDF p.16 / p.1271]
Religion and gender diversity [PDF p.17 / p.1272]
reviewer_flags: COE minimum is negative (-0.057) [Table 2, PDF p.10 / p.1265]
WACC effect is insignificant within firms (FEM t=-1.34); significance comes from GLS [Table 5, PDF p.13 / p.1268]
Table 4: the FEM and REM columns are identical to three decimals for every variable [PDF p.12 / p.1267]
Table 4: OLS SDG coefficient (t=-2.48) carries no significance star [PDF p.12 / p.1267]
The COVID dummy (=2021) is the only time control in a 3-year panel [Table 1, PDF p.9 / p.1264]
Sample selected on end-2023 market cap, i.e. ex-post selection [PDF p.6 / p.1261]
FSIZE-LEV correlation 0.7 [PDF p.10 / p.1265]
[INFERENCE] The WACC regression on LEV is partly mechanical, since WACC is built from LEV-dependent weights

papers.title: Tac dong cua cong bo thong tin phat trien ben vung toi chi phi su dung von chu so huu cua cac doanh nghiep cong nghiep nang luong tren TTCK Viet Nam (The impact of sustainable disclosure on the cost of equity of energy enterprises on the Vietnamese stock market)
papers.source: Tap chi Khoa hoc va Cong nghe Truong Dai hoc Cong nghiep Ha Noi (HaUI Journal of Science and Technology), Vol. 61 No. 6, pp. 138-146 (Vietnamese)
papers.topic: GRI-based sustainability disclosure and cost of equity in the energy industry
papers.research_question: What is the effect of sustainability disclosure on the cost of equity of listed energy firms? [PDF p.1-2 / p.138-139]
papers.abstract: 58 energy firms (HOSE, HNX, UPCOM), 2019-2023, 290 observations; sustainability disclosure has a positive effect on cost of equity, attributed to short-run compliance and reporting costs. [PDF p.1 / p.138]
hypotheses: H1: SD disclosure negatively affects cost of equity [PDF p.4 / p.141]
papers.data_source: FiinPro-X (financial data); hand-coded FS, annual and sustainability reports; Rf from Damodaran's website [PDF p.4-5 / p.141-142]
papers.sample: 58 energy firms on HOSE/HNX/UPCOM, 2019-2023, 290 firm-years (balanced) [PDF p.5 / p.142]
dependent_vars: RE: CAPM, Rf = nominal 10-year government bond yield (Damodaran), beta = cov/var vs market [PDF p.4 / p.141]
independent_vars: PTBVDN: average of 77 binary GRI items (15 of which appear in the Circular 155 appendix) [PDF p.4 / p.141]
papers.method: OLS, REM, FEM; F-test and Hausman (p=0.0000, FEM preferred); VIF, Wald, Wooldridge; robust SE and GMM said to be applied [PDF p.5-7 / p.142-144]
papers.econometric_model: RE = b0 + b1*PTBVDN + b2*SIZE + b3*ROE + b4*QM + b5*KT + b6*LEV (no firm or year subscripts shown, no year effects) [PDF p.4 / p.141]
main_findings: Authors conclude a positive effect [PDF p.6-7 / p.143-144]
Mean disclosure rises from 0.163 (2019) to 0.188 (2023); max 0.571 [Table 1, PDF p.5 / p.142]
Mean COE falls from 9.21% (2019) to 6.88% (2021), then rises to 11.72% (2023); negative minima [Table 2, PDF p.6 / p.143]
papers.direction_disclosure_COE: Positive (as claimed; insignificant in the Hausman-preferred FEM)
robustness: Robust SE and GMM described as applied, but no results are reported [PDF p.7 / p.144]
limitations_explicit: No limitations section; disclosure quality and credibility are discussed as a practical issue [PDF p.7 / p.144]
future_research: Other industries; dividend growth model for COE; effect on cost of debt [PDF p.8 / p.145]
reviewer_flags: The headline positive effect is insignificant in the Hausman-preferred FEM (p=0.452); it is significant only in OLS and REM [Table 3, PDF p.6 / p.143]
Robust/GMM estimates claimed but not shown [PDF p.7 / p.144]
F-test described as choosing between OLS and REM [PDF p.5 / p.142]
No year effects, while disclosure trends up and COE moves sharply with macro conditions [Tables 1-2]
Negative COE observations [Table 2, PDF p.6 / p.143]
[INFERENCE] Common upward trends in disclosure and COE over 2021-2023, with no year effects, can produce a positive pooled correlation

papers.title: Research on the Impact of Governance Structure on the Cost of Equity Capital of Food Businesses Listed on the Vietnam Stock Market
authors: Thuy Thi Pham (University of Labour and Social Affairs)
papers.source: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews, Vol. 4 No. 12, pp. 3085-3095
papers.topic: Board and CEO governance structure and cost of equity
papers.research_question: How does governance structure affect the cost of equity of listed food-processing firms? [PDF p.1 / p.3085]
papers.abstract: 55 listed food firms, 2015-2022; governance measured by board independence, CEO duality, CEO tenure, board meetings and nomination committee; stronger governance lowers COE. [PDF p.1 / p.3085]
theory: Stewardship theory, called 'management theory' (Davis et al. 1997), mentioned as the competing view [PDF p.9-10 / p.3093-3094]
hypotheses: H2-H12: expected signs in Table 1 (board size -, independence -, DUAL +, committee -, tenure -, meetings -) [PDF p.4 / p.3088]
papers.data_source: Annual reports (governance, hand-collected CEO tenure); FiinGroup (monthly prices); VNINDEX; 5- and 10-year bond yields [PDF p.2 / p.3086]
papers.sample: 55 food-processing listed firms, 2015-2022; 440 firm-years described, 341 used in regressions [PDF p.2, 6-9 / p.3086, 3090-3093]
dependent_vars: COE: CAPM; Rf = 10-year bond; monthly rolling beta (12 observations), annualised [PDF p.2-3 / p.3086-3087]
independent_vars: DUAL (coded 0 if CEO is chair, 1 if separate)
papers.method: Pooled OLS, REM, FEM; BP-LM (p=0.3289), F-test (p=0.0000), Hausman (p=0.0211); Wald and Wooldridge; FE with clustered SE [PDF p.7-9 / p.3091-3093]
papers.econometric_model: COE = a + b1 Size + b2 Liquid + b3 ROA + b4 Growth + b5 Boardp + b6 Dual + b7 Tenure + b8 Lev + b9 Meet + b10 Board.size + b11 Renumer + e [PDF p.4 / p.3088]
main_findings: Final FE (clustered): BOARD.SIZE -0.064 (p=0.065), RENUMER -0.455 (p=0.083), DUAL +0.215 (p=0.077); BOARDP, TENURE, MEET n.s. [Table 8, PDF p.9 / p.3093]
R-squared 0.114, N=341 [Table 8]
robustness: None beyond model selection and clustering
reviewer_flags: DUAL = 1 means separate roles [PDF p.2 / p.3086], so the positive coefficient implies that separation raises COE; the paper reads it as 'duality raises COE' [PDF p.9 / p.3093]
COE mean 0.38 with range -0.811 to 1.308 [Table 2, PDF p.5 / p.3089]
440 observations described, 341 used, with no explanation
Mean board size 5.748 [Table 2], but the text says the average is 7 [PDF p.10 / p.3094]
GROWTH 95% CI [.542, .546] excludes its own coefficient .294 [Table 8, PDF p.9 / p.3093]
'F test that all u_i=0: F(12,269)' implies 13 panel units, inconsistent with 55 firms [Table 5, PDF p.7 / p.3091] [INFERENCE on df]
Interviews are mentioned as the basis for adding variables, but no interview method is described [PDF p.1 / p.3085]
Of six governance variables only three are significant, and only at 10%; the conclusion of a general negative effect overstates the evidence

papers.title: The impact of corporate social responsibility on the cost of equity: an analysis of Vietnamese listed companies
authors: Thy Ha Van Le (Quy Nhon University)
papers.source: Investment Management and Financial Innovations, 16(3), 87-96 (Business Perspectives)
papers.page_map: printed page = PDF page + 85 (PDF p.1 is a cover sheet)
papers.topic: Environmental disclosure and ex-ante cost of equity
papers.research_question: What is the effect of environmental disclosure on the cost of equity of Vietnamese listed firms? [PDF p.3 / p.88]
papers.abstract: 115 non-financial firms, 2014-2017, 460 observations; GRI content analysis; Easton (2004)-type ex-ante COE; FEM shows a significant negative relation. [PDF p.2 / p.87]
theory: No formal theory section; social-contract/stakeholder information role of disclosure (Gray et al. 1995) [PDF p.3 / p.88]
Literature review lists explanations for positive findings: decoupling of disclosure and behaviour, negative-NPV CSR investment, lack of trust [PDF p.4 / p.89]
hypotheses: Environmental disclosure has a negative impact on cost of equity [PDF p.5 / p.90]
papers.data_source: Vietnamese annual reports (hand-coded); market data (source not specified) [PDF p.5-6 / p.90-91]
papers.sample: 115 non-financial listed firms each year 2014-2017 (460 firm-years); random sampling; food 26, aquatic 22, energy 14, others [Table 2, PDF p.5 / p.90]
dependent_vars: COE = forecast EPS(t+1) / average price after the report date (labelled an adjusted Easton 2004 PEG model) [PDF p.6 / p.91]
independent_vars: CED: environmental disclosure index, binary GRI (G4) items / expected items [PDF p.6 / p.91; PDF p.10 / p.95]
papers.method: REM and FEM; Hausman (p=0.0055) selects FEM; Wald test; XTSCC (Driscoll-Kraay) SE [PDF p.8-9 / p.93-94]
papers.econometric_model: COE_it = b0 + b1*CED_it + SIZE + LEV + LTG + LIQUID + SOE + FOR + BETA + e_it [Eq 3, PDF p.7 / p.92]
main_findings: REM: CED -62.49 (t=-1.66, marked **) [Table 6, PDF p.8 / p.93]
FEM: CED -45.17 (t=-1.16, n.s.) [Table 6]
FEM with XTSCC SE: CED -45.17*** (t=-6.93) [Table 7, PDF p.9 / p.94]
SOE and FOR positive, LEV and BETA positive, SIZE negative under XTSCC [Table 7]
38 firms disclosed environmental information in 2014, 115 in 2017 [PDF p.8 / p.93]
limitations_explicit: Small sample (n=115), not highly representative [PDF p.10 / p.95]
GRI G4 criteria not all suited to Vietnam [PDF p.10 / p.95]
future_research: Build an environmental disclosure index on Circular 155 [PDF p.10 / p.95]
reviewer_flags: The text says REM shows a positive significant relation [PDF p.8 / p.93]; Table 6 shows a negative coefficient (-62.49)
REM t=-1.66 is marked ** (5%) although |t| < 1.96 [Table 6]
The coefficient goes from insignificant (t=-1.16) to t=-6.93 purely through the standard-error change, with T=4 [INFERENCE: Driscoll-Kraay SE are unreliable with very short T]
The 'PEG' measure is in fact a forward earnings yield; COE mean 135.46, min -414.1, max 1015.3, units unclear [Table 4, PDF p.7 / p.92]
The title says CSR, but only environmental disclosure is measured
[INFERENCE] Disclosure rises from 38 to 115 disclosing firms across the Circular 155 effective period, so much of the CED variation is regulation-driven; this is not exploited

papers.title: The mediating effect of stock price crash risk on the relationship between corporate social responsibility and cost of equity moderated by state ownership: Moderated-mediation analysis
authors: Nguyen Thanh Liem (University of Economics and Law, VNU-HCM)
papers.source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management, 29(5), 1384-1395 (Wiley); received Dec 2021, accepted Mar 2022
papers.topic: CSR disclosure and implied cost of equity: crash-risk mediation and state-ownership moderation
papers.research_question: Does stock price crash risk mediate, and does state ownership moderate, the CSR disclosure-COE relation? [PDF p.2 / p.1385]
papers.abstract: 225 Vietnamese listed non-financial firms; GMM and Sobel tests; crash risk is a complementary mediator; abstract states that state ownership strengthens the negative CSR-COE effect. [PDF p.1 / p.1384]
theory: Investor base / socially conscious investors (Mohr et al.)
SOE multitask theory (Bai et al. 2006) vs SOE inefficiency [PDF p.2-3 / p.1385-1386]
hypotheses: H1: CSR disclosure negatively affects COE
H2: crash risk mediates the CSR-COE relation
H3: state ownership moderates such that the negative relation is stronger when state ownership is higher [PDF p.3-4 / p.1386-1387]
papers.data_source: Annual and sustainable development reports (hand-coded CSR); Refinitiv Eikon (state ownership, financials); prices for crash risk [PDF p.4 / p.1387]
papers.sample: 225 non-financial firms with CSR disclosure data 2014-2019, 1,340 firm-years; industry leaders covering >=90% of industry assets; GMM N=816 [PDF p.4 / p.1387; Table 2]
dependent_vars: COE: implied, Easton (2004) model with Harris & Wang (2013) cross-sectional earnings forecasts [PDF p.4 / p.1387; Appendix A, PDF p.12 / p.1395]
independent_vars: CSRD: 33 binary GRI-2016 criteria (6 economic, 8 environmental, 19 social) [PDF p.5 / p.1388]
moderators: SOE: % state ownership; mean-centred interaction CSRD x SOE [PDF p.5 / p.1388]
controls: INDUSTRY dummies (no year effects reported) [PDF p.5 / p.1388]
papers.method: System GMM with lagged COE; Baron-Kenny three-step mediation; Sobel / delta / Monte Carlo tests; Hansen and AR(2) diagnostics [PDF p.5-8 / p.1388-1391]
papers.econometric_model: COE_it = a + b*CSRD_it (+ g*CRASH_it) (+ SOE, CSRD x SOE) + controls + INDUSTRY + e_it [Eqs 1-7, PDF p.4 / p.1387]
main_findings: CSRD -0.065*** on COE (t=-5.27), N=816 [Table 2, PDF p.7 / p.1390; signs verified on rendered page]
CSRD -0.204*** on CRASH; CRASH +0.142*** on COE; CSRD -0.067*** with CRASH included [Table 3, PDF p.8 / p.1391]
Sobel indirect effect -0.006 (p=0.029), 18.5% of total effect [Table 4, PDF p.8 / p.1391]
Mean COE 10.8%, mean CSRD 0.263 [Table 1, PDF p.6 / p.1389]
robustness: Three Sobel variants (delta, Sobel, Monte Carlo) [Table 4]
Hansen and AR(2) tests in every GMM column
limitations_explicit: Non-financial firms from one developing market; may not generalise across institutional settings [PDF p.10 / p.1393]
future_research: Replicate in other developing countries; state-owned firms in high-polluting industries; cross-national samples [PDF p.10 / p.1393]
reviewer_flags: Abstract and H3 say state ownership STRENGTHENS the negative CSR-COE effect [PDF p.1 / p.1384; PDF p.3-4 / p.1386-1387]; Table 5 shows a POSITIVE interaction with a negative main effect, i.e. attenuation, and the conclusion says 'attenuate' / 'mixed moderating role' [PDF p.9 / p.1392]
The SOE and interaction coefficients are reported as 0.000, so economic magnitude cannot be assessed [Table 5]
Adding the mediator makes the direct effect LARGER in magnitude (-0.065 to -0.067) [Table 3], which is inconsistent with a negative indirect path through CRASH
The product of Table 3 paths (-0.204 x 0.142 = -0.029) does not match the Sobel indirect effect (-0.006), and Table 4's total/direct effects (0.033/0.027) do not match Table 3 (0.065/0.067)
No year effects reported; the 2014-2019 window straddles Circular 155, which the paper calls 'the most essential document for regulating CSR in Vietnam' [PDF p.2 / p.1385] but does not exploit
[INFERENCE] 100-120 instruments for 225 firms: below the groups count, but near the level where instrument proliferation weakens the Hansen test
Negative-earnings firms are dropped from the Easton estimation [Appendix A], which is a selection on profitability

papers.title: Impact of Corporate Disclosure on Cost of Equity Capital in Vietnam
authors: Lan Thi Ngoc Nguyen (Foreign Trade University, Hanoi)
papers.source: International Journal of Financial Research, 8(4), 64-70 (Sciedu Press)
papers.topic: General (annual-report) corporate disclosure and implied cost of equity
papers.research_question: Does disclosing more information reduce the cost of equity of firms listed in Vietnam? [PDF p.1 / p.64]
papers.abstract: Botosan (1997) disclosure score and residual-income implied COE; disclosure has a significant reducing effect on COE. [PDF p.1 / p.64]
theory: Public/private information structure (Easley & O'Hara 2004; Kim & Verrecchia) [PDF p.1-2 / p.64-65]
hypotheses: Implicit: disclosure lowers COE (no formal hypothesis numbering)
papers.data_source: FiinPro (StoxPlus): 2015 annual reports, accounting and price data [PDF p.4 / p.67]
papers.sample: 225 non-financial HOSE-listed firms, cross-section, financial year 2015 [PDF p.4 / p.67]
dependent_vars: IMPLIED: residual-income implied COE, 2-year horizon, self-generated forecasts (growth = ROE x plowback), prices 3 months after year-end [PDF p.3-4 / p.66-67]
independent_vars: DSCORE: Botosan (1997) annual-report disclosure index, 105 points [PDF p.2-4 / p.65-67]
papers.method: Cross-sectional OLS with White-Huber SE; stepwise and rank regression robustness [PDF p.5-6 / p.68-69]
papers.econometric_model: IMPLIED_i = a + b1 DSCORE_i + b2 BETA_i + b3 PB_i + b4 LnMCAP_i + e_i [Eq 4, PDF p.5 / p.68]
main_findings: Beta insignificant (-0.0045, p=0.672); beta-implied COE correlation -0.0266 n.s. [Tables 2-3, PDF p.5 / p.68]
LnMCAP +0.0067** (size raises implied COE), attributed to mispricing [PDF p.5-6 / p.68-69]
Mean disclosure 27/105; mean implied COE 14.84% [Table 1, PDF p.4 / p.67]
Rank regression: rankDSCORE -0.2641*** [Table 4, PDF p.6 / p.69]
limitations_explicit: None stated as a section; notes that analyst forecasts are unavailable in Vietnam, so forecasts are self-generated [PDF p.3 / p.66]
reviewer_flags: Single-year cross-section; disclosure policy assumed 'quite stable over time' without evidence [PDF p.4 / p.67]
[INFERENCE] Self-generated forecasts (ROE x plowback) tie the implied COE mechanically to profitability and payout, which may correlate with disclosure
No endogeneity treatment; only three controls
Explicitly argues CAPM cannot test a disclosure effect [PDF p.3 / p.66], which directly bears on P1-P4, P9

papers.title: Impact of corporate governance attributes on cost of equity: Evidence from an emerging economy
papers.source: Managerial Auditing Journal (Emerald), online-first version (no volume/page numbers in the PDF)
papers.page_map: no printed page numbers; cite PDF pages (PDF p.1 = Emerald cover sheet)
papers.topic: Composite corporate governance index and cost of equity (India)
papers.research_question: Does a comprehensive Indian corporate governance index (post-Companies Act 2013) lower the cost of equity? [PDF p.2]
papers.abstract: S&P BSE 500 firms 2001-2016; 43-attribute, 7-sub-index CGI; negative significant CGI-COE relation; board composition and audit committee sub-indices matter. [PDF p.2]
theory: Law-and-finance / investor protection (La Porta et al. 1998) [PDF p.7]
hypotheses: H1: corporate governance has a negative impact on the cost of equity [PDF p.7]
papers.data_source: CMIE ProwessIQ; hand-collected governance from annual reports [PDF p.8]
papers.sample: 319 non-financial S&P BSE 500 firms with March fiscal year-end, 2001-2016, 5,104 firm-years (balanced; missing data interpolated/extrapolated) [PDF p.8]
dependent_vars: COE (%): MEASUREMENT NOT DEFINED anywhere in the paper (verified by full-text search)
independent_vars: CGI: 43 binary items scored 1 only if ABOVE the mandatory minimum; 7 equally weighted sub-indices (board composition, board activities, audit committee, shareholders' grievance, nomination & remuneration, ownership structure, cross-listing) [PDF p.9, 11-13; Table I]
papers.method: Pooled OLS (Hausman p=0.0695 favours RE; BP-LM p=1.000 favours pooled OLS) [PDF p.15]
papers.econometric_model: COE = a + b1 CGI + b2 Lever + b3 MTBR + b4 LogAssets + b5 BoardSize + b6 SaleGrowth + Industry + e [PDF p.11]
main_findings: CGI -0.089 (p=0.021); R-squared 0.083 [Table III, PDF p.15; signs verified on rendered page]
Board composition -0.068 (p=0.036); audit committee -0.061 (p=0.035); ownership structure -0.130 (p=0.049); other sub-indices n.s. [Table III]
Only market-to-book significant among controls [PDF p.11]
robustness: CGI regressed on ROA and PE ratio (not a robustness test of the COE result) [PDF p.11; Table III]
future_research: Use the index to study other valuation and profitability measures [PDF p.18]
reviewer_flags: The dependent variable's construction is never described
Claims a 'causal relationship' [PDF p.2] from pooled OLS
Text credits 'fixed effects regression models' [PDF p.16] though pooled OLS is the reported model
Missing data interpolated/extrapolated; index-replacement firms filled with prior constituents' data [PDF p.8]
Ownership-structure sub-index is significant in Table III but not mentioned in the abstract or discussion
Above-mandatory scoring [PDF p.9] is a design precedent for separating compliance from voluntary practice (relevant to G6/G13)

papers.title: The Impact of Corporate Governance on the Cost of Equity: Empirical Evidence from Pakistani Listed Companies
authors: Safdar Ali Butt (Mohammad Ali Jinnah University, Islamabad)
papers.page_map: printed page = PDF page + 138 (PDF metadata title is wrong: 'Apple market integration')
papers.topic: Governance attributes and a governance score vs CAPM cost of equity (Pakistan)
papers.research_question: Does corporate governance quality affect the cost of equity of Pakistani listed firms? [PDF p.2-3 / p.140-141]
papers.abstract: 114 KSE firms 2003-2007; CAPM COE; managerial ownership and board size negative; board independence, audit committee independence and the governance score positive. [PDF p.1 / p.139]
theory: Signalling of investor protection (Himmelberg et al.) [PDF p.4-5 / p.142-143]
Investor-protection substitution/complementarity (Klapper & Love 2002; Chen et al. 2004) [PDF p.6, 8 / p.144, 146]
hypotheses: H0: governance does not affect cost of capital; H1: it does [PDF p.10 / p.148]
papers.data_source: Annual reports, State Bank of Pakistan balance-sheet review, company websites, direct contact [PDF p.9 / p.147]
papers.sample: 114 non-financial KSE firms across 15 sectors (57 textile spinning), 2003-2007; 541-558 obs [PDF p.9 / p.147; Tables 5-10]
dependent_vars: Ke: CAPM, beta from 2 years of monthly returns [PDF p.11 / p.149]
independent_vars: Individual: ownership concentration, managerial ownership, board independence, audit committee independence, board size
CGS: weighted score (INED presence 55%, ownership 45%) [Appendix B, PDF p.32 / p.170]
papers.method: OLS; LSDV with industry dummies ('fixed effects') and with industry + year dummies [PDF p.12-22 / p.150-160]
papers.econometric_model: Ke_it = a + b1 Fsize + b2 OC + b3 MO + b4 BI + b5 ACI + b6 BS + b7 ROE (+ industry, year dummies) + u_it [PDF p.13 / p.151]
main_findings: OLS: only size significant (-0.0094, t=-3.24); R-squared 0.034 [Table 4, PDF p.13 / p.151]
Industry + year dummies: board size -0.017 (p=0.088); size -0.0078 (p=0.018); OC, MO, BI, ACI, ROE n.s. [Table 6, PDF p.17 / p.155]
Year dummies large and negative (2007: -0.287, p<0.001) [Table 6]
limitations_explicit: Governance score limited by unavailability of published data on many governance aspects [PDF p.25 / p.163]
future_research: More variables in the governance score; estimate Ke with other models [PDF p.25 / p.163]
reviewer_flags: Conclusion 'good corporate governance reduces a company's cost of equity' [PDF p.25 / p.163] is not supported: the governance score is positive and insignificant, and only board size is marginal
The discussion of managerial ownership contradicts itself ('negative impact ... i.e. higher ownership leads to higher COE') [PDF p.23 / p.161]
Table 2 maximum and minimum rows are swapped; Ke ranges from -0.93 to 1.91 (negative CAPM COE again) [PDF p.11 / p.149]
'Fixed effects' are industry dummies, not firm effects
Measurement-validity insight: Pakistani firms label all non-executive directors as independent, so BI may carry no information [PDF p.23 / p.161]
